  In the 1860s, French makers added cranks and pedals to the front wheel. This
  machine was the velocipede, and people called it the "boneshaker" because the
  iron-rimmed wheels made the ride hard. In the 1870s, makers built the
  high-wheeler, or penny-farthing. One turn of the pedals moved the bike far,
  because the front wheel was very large. But a fall from the high seat was
  dangerous.                                  

  In 1885, John Kemp Starley made the Rover "safety bicycle". It had two wheels 
  of equal size and a chain that drove the rear wheel. In 1888, John Boyd Dunlop
  added the air-filled tire, and the ride became soft and fast. Women and men
  of all ages began to ride, and the bicycle changed how people travelled and
  worked.     

  In the 20th century, makers added gears, light alloy frames, and later carbon
  fibre. Today the bicycle is a common tool for transport, sport, and clean city
  travel.
